description: Fig. 1 is a single-panel schematic temperature–time schedule (heat-treatment diagram) for the experimental Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel. The y-axis is labelled "Temperature" and the x-axis "Time"; neither axis carries numeric tick values, so every temperature is known only from printed annotations. The route runs left to right in four stages. (1) A heating ramp to a flat plateau labelled "Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h", followed on the descending limb by a sawtooth (zigzag) segment labelled "Hot rolling", then a straight fall labelled "Air cooling" to Room temperature. (2) A second plateau labelled "1050 °C for 1 h" (stated in the citing text to lie in the ferrite + austenite dual-phase region), terminated by a labelled "Water quenching" step. (3) A third plateau labelled "Annealing for 1 h", whose top edge is annotated "800 °C" and whose interior carries a dashed vertical marker annotated "620 °C", denoting the 620–800 °C annealing window, closed by "Air cooling" to "Room temperature". A horizontal dashed line labelled "Ac1 = 617 °C" spans the diagram, lying just below the 620 °C threshold. The figure defines the full homogenization → hot rolling → air cooling → 1050 °C reheat → water quench → 1 h anneal → air cooling processing path whose variants are sampled as HR, IQ-1050 and QA-620/680/740/800.

observations.observation: The diagram's vertical axis is labelled 'Temperature' and the horizontal axis 'Time'; no numeric tick values are printed on either axis, so it is a qualitative schedule.
A horizontal dashed line spanning the whole diagram is annotated 'Ac1 = 617 °C'.
The first (highest) plateau is annotated 'Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h'.
A sawtooth/zigzag segment on the descending limb after homogenization is annotated 'Hot rolling', indicating rolling during cooling rather than an isothermal hold.
The cooling segment after hot rolling is annotated 'Air cooling' and terminates at 'Room temperature'.
The second plateau is annotated '1050 °C for 1 h'.
The step following the 1050 °C hold is annotated 'Water quenching'.

The third plateau is annotated 'Annealing for 1 h' with '800 °C' printed at its top edge and a dashed vertical marker annotated '620 °C' inside it, indicating an annealing temperature window of 620–800 °C.
The final segment after annealing is annotated 'Air cooling' leading to 'Room temperature'.
The 620 °C annealing marker lies just above the Ac1 = 617 °C dashed reference line, so the annealing window is drawn essentially at/above Ac1.
The caption states this is the schematic diagram of the thermal treatment for the experimental steel.

The citing text states the ingot was heated to 1100 °C for 2 h, forged to 80 mm × 70 mm, reheated to 1100 °C for 2 h and hot rolled from 80 to 12 mm in eight passes with initial rolling temperature ~1050 °C and finishing rolling temperature ~950 °C, then air cooled (sample HR) — the 8-pass rolling detail and 950 °C finishing temperature are not visible in the schematic.
The citing text states the hot-rolled plate was reheated to 1050 °C, located in the ferrite and austenite dual-phase region, for 1 h followed by water quenching (sample IQ-1050).

The citing text states the water-quenched plate was annealed for 1 h at 620 °C, 680 °C, 740 °C and 800 °C, giving samples QA-620, QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800; the schematic shows only the 620 and 800 °C end-members of this range.

subfigures.description: Single-panel schematic temperature–time (heat-treatment) diagram. Qualitative axes labelled 'Temperature' (vertical) and 'Time' (horizontal) with no numeric ticks. Shows homogenization plateau at 1100 °C for 2 h, a sawtooth 'Hot rolling' segment on the cooling limb, 'Air cooling' to Room temperature, a second plateau at '1050 °C for 1 h', 'Water quenching', an 'Annealing for 1 h' plateau annotated 800 °C at its top with a dashed 620 °C marker inside, then 'Air cooling' to 'Room temperature'. A dashed horizontal reference line is labelled 'Ac1 = 617 °C'.
